questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Firstly, it was important for me to chose a university that offered courses within the field of my current studies and career. Furthermore, i emphasized choosing a well-respected university by virtue of an international respected and acknowledged place.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. However i had to reach out to my coordinator at the host university myself to get the final details.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got an e-mail with most of the information needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult, i was alerted early in the proces that they did not have a lot of campus housing and that they would not assist with finding housing outside of campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Finding housing in Rotterdam is a widespread problem, both from my own experience and from other students that i met during my exchange. Many landlords, real estate agents etc. do no allow students in their rentals. Furthermore, housing is really expensive in many places.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy and flexible - however the information given beforehand about the courses and how to chose/check timetables etc. was not very informative.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was only one person, the coordinator at my host university, to guide all the exchange students. I did sometimes to reach other people at the university but they kept on referring to the coordinator which made it difficult when he was out of office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I did not experience any problems with this.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to take the time needed to learn how to chose the right courses - it is your own responsibility to make sure there is no overlaps etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level of courses similar to the ones at my home university. However, some courses which had same amount of ECTS points was disproportionate by means of assignments, preparation etc.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a big difference. At my host university the lectures consisted mostly of class discussions and individual participation in contrary to my home university. Furthermore, there is only final exams (100% weight) at my home university whereas grade at my host university was based on assignments, in-class participation, presentations etc. during the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Research and writing skills, Mediation Advocacy, Commercial contracts and Corporate and white collar crime.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I personally found commercial contracts very interesting and useful for my further studies at home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of activities, but i was hard to find and thus engage in these in the beginning since there was no real introduction or information given.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did attend any why i have nothing to add.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to Den Haag. It is only 40 minute by train from Rotterdam, and is a very nice and beautiful city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy since the culture in the Netherlands is quite similar to the danish culture in my opinion.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I learned quickly to seek and interact with the locals in classes myself.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing further to add.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found the locals very open-minded and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: (1) Make sure to keep up in class. The host university does not give days off with the purpose of reading as they do at the home university. (2) Seek other people in the beginning especially, people quickly find their friends and that only happens if you interact with others yourself (3) Engage in the non-academic student activities - i only heard good things about many of their events and it is a golden opportunity to meet new people - maybe even someone from other studies.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have nothing further to add.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to meet a lot of new people from all around the globe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning. I expected some kind of introduction days where the exchange students would get to know each other or at least that i would get some kind of information on where to contact and find other exchange students. We had one introduction day, but it was merely formal and not as much getting-to-know-eachother as i would have hoped and expected. Because of this i did not know who to reach out to in the first couple of weeks since i did not have any names or information on the others.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
